outputs.L3:
The memory device includes a plurality of bank groups, and each bank group includes one or more memory banks. These bank groups are coupled to both a first bus and a second bus, which are used to transmit command and address information within the memory device.

The memory device further includes a toggle signal generation unit. This unit generates a first signal that toggles in response to a column command signal, such as a read command or a write command. The toggle signal generation unit also generates a second signal having a logic value opposite to that of the first signal. Accordingly, when the first signal is active, the second signal is inactive, and when the second signal is active, the first signal is inactive.

A column command transmission unit is configured to transmit column command signals, including read command signals and write command signals, to one of the first and second buses based on the states of the first and second signals. Specifically, when the first signal is active, the column command transmission unit transmits the read or write command signal to the first bus. When the second signal is active, the column command transmission unit transmits the read or write command signal to the second bus.

The memory device also includes a column address transmission unit. The column address transmission unit transmits a column address signal corresponding to the read or write command signal to the same bus to which that command signal is transmitted. Thus, when the read or write command signal is transmitted to the first bus, the corresponding column address signal is also transmitted to the first bus. Likewise, when the read or write command signal is transmitted to the second bus, the corresponding column address signal is also transmitted to the second bus.

By alternately transmitting column command signals and their corresponding column address signals through the first and second buses, the memory device can efficiently distribute command and address traffic among the plurality of bank groups.

A memory device architecture for bank-group access includes a command and address routing structure that uses two separate internal buses to convey column-related information within the memory device. In this architecture, read and write column commands, together with their corresponding column addresses, are not routed through a single shared path. Instead, a toggle-signal generator produces a toggle signal that controls how the column commands and column addresses are assigned to a first bus and a second bus.

During operation, the toggle signal alternates between states so that successive column command/address sets are routed to different buses. For example, when the toggle signal is in a first state, a read or write column command and its associated column address may be transmitted on the first bus. When the toggle signal changes to a second state, the next read or write column command and its associated column address may be transmitted on the second bus. By repeatedly switching the routing selection in this manner, the memory device distributes column access traffic across both buses rather than concentrating all column command and address traffic on one bus.

The first and second buses may be coupled to command decoding circuitry, address latching circuitry, and bank-group control circuitry associated with multiple memory bank groups. Each bank group may include a plurality of memory banks, and the routed column commands may identify read or write operations directed to selected banks within selected bank groups. The corresponding column addresses identify the column locations within the selected memory array portions. By coordinating the toggle signal with the incoming command stream, the architecture ensures that each column command remains paired with the correct column address as the information is transferred through the device.

This dual-bus arrangement improves command routing efficiency in memory devices that support frequent accesses to multiple bank groups. In conventional routing schemes that rely heavily on a single internal bus, column commands and column addresses may compete for the same routing resources, particularly when back-to-back read and write operations are issued. Such contention can create timing pressure, require additional arbitration, or limit the rate at which commands can be delivered to the appropriate bank-group circuitry. By alternating traffic between the first and second buses, the described architecture reduces congestion on any one bus and allows command/address information to be delivered more efficiently.

The toggle-signal generator may be implemented using sequential logic, such as a flip-flop or counter-based circuit, that changes state in response to received column commands, clock signals, or command-valid indications. In some implementations, the toggle signal may switch state for each qualifying read or write column command. In other implementations, the toggle behavior may be synchronized with specific memory timing requirements, burst operations, or bank-group access patterns. The routing circuitry may include multiplexers, demultiplexers, switches, or gating logic controlled by the toggle signal to select whether a particular command/address pair is driven onto the first bus or the second bus.

Because the command and address traffic is distributed across multiple buses, the memory device can more effectively support high-throughput operation in systems with multiple bank groups. The architecture may reduce internal bus contention, simplify timing closure for command distribution paths, and improve the ability of the memory device to process consecutive column operations. As a result, read and write accesses can be routed to the appropriate bank groups with improved efficiency, supporting increased memory bandwidth and more reliable operation in advanced memory systems.

Computers, smartphones, cameras, and many other electronic devices need memory devices to work properly. Without them, it would be difficult to save documents, photos, videos, music, or software.

There are different types of memory devices. Some are internal, such as a hard disk drive, solid-state drive, or RAM. Others are external, such as a USB flash drive, memory card, or external hard drive. Each type has its own purpose. For example, RAM helps a computer run programs quickly, while a USB flash drive is useful for carrying files from one place to another.

A memory device can store different amounts of data depending on its capacity. Older devices could only store a small amount of information, but modern memory devices can store gigabytes or even terabytes of data. They have also become smaller, faster, and more reliable over time.

Memory devices are used in daily life by students, workers, businesses, and many other people. They help us keep important information safe and make it easy to access data whenever we need it. For this reason, a memory device is one of the most essential tools in the digital world.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in patent language, a memory device architecture including bank groups connected to two buses and circuitry that distributes column commands and addresses alternately across the buses.
counterfactuals.output:
A memory device comprises a memory array partitioned into a plurality of bank groups, each bank group including a plurality of memory banks addressable by column commands. The memory device further comprises a first command/address bus and a second command/address bus extending to the plurality of bank groups, and command distribution circuitry coupled between an external command/address interface and the first and second command/address buses.

The command distribution circuitry is configured to receive a sequence of column commands and associated column addresses from the external command/address interface and to distribute the sequence alternately between the first and second command/address buses. In one embodiment, a first column command and corresponding column address are driven on the first command/address bus for execution by a selected bank group, and a next column command and corresponding column address are driven on the second command/address bus for execution by a selected bank group. The alternating distribution may continue for successive column command/address pairs, thereby reducing loading on each bus and permitting temporally adjacent column operations to be conveyed over different buses.

Each bank group may include bus selection circuitry, decoding circuitry, or both, configured to receive column command/address information from at least one of the first and second command/address buses. The bus selection circuitry may select a bus based on a bank group address, a column command phase, a toggle state, or a command allocation signal generated by the command distribution circuitry. In certain embodiments, different bank groups are coupled to both buses, while in other embodiments a subset of bank groups is primarily associated with the first command/address bus and another subset of bank groups is primarily associated with the second command/address bus.

The command distribution circuitry may include a toggle circuit, counter, flip-flop, arbiter, or scheduler configured to alternate assignment of column commands between the first and second command/address buses. The circuitry may be further configured to maintain correspondence between each column command and its associated column address, such that the command and address of a given column access are transmitted on a same one of the first and second command/address buses.

In operation, upon receipt of consecutive column access requests, the memory device routes a first column access request to the first command/address bus and routes a second column access request to the second command/address bus. The selected bank groups decode the received command/address information and perform corresponding column operations, including read or write operations, on addressed memory cells. Alternating distribution of column commands and addresses across the two buses reduces command/address bus contention, decreases capacitive loading per bus, and improves command bandwidth within the memory device.
